first-repository-and-commits.r: A developer committed forty files with the message 'update'. Months later nobody could tell which change broke the build. Small commits with clear messages let the team find the exact change in minutes.
first-repository-and-commits.x: History is documentation. Write commits that explain why, keep them focused so they can be reviewed and reverted alone, and keep generated files and secrets out of the repository from the start.

staging-undoing-and-stashing.r: Someone ran a hard reset to remove a bad commit and also lost an hour of uncommitted work. Choosing restore, revert or reset deliberately, and stashing work first, would have saved it.
staging-undoing-and-stashing.x: Choose the undo by who else has the commit. Rewriting shared history hurts others, so revert it; rewrite only your own local work. Know what reflog can recover and for how long.

branches-and-merging.r: Two engineers changed the same function on different branches and the merge produced conflict markers that were committed by accident. A short branch life and an automated check for conflict markers prevented the repeat.
branches-and-merging.x: Long-lived branches create merge pain and hidden risk. Keep branches short, integrate often and decide whether you want merge commits or a linear history, then enforce it with settings, not memory.

rebase-and-clean-history.r: A teammate rebased a branch that others had already pulled, and the team spent a morning reconciling duplicate commits. The rule of never rewriting shared history became part of the contributing guide.
rebase-and-clean-history.x: Rebase is a tool for your own work before sharing. Use it to make history readable, but protect shared branches from force pushes and use force-with-lease when you must.

remotes-fetch-pull-and-push.r: An engineer pulled with the default settings and created a surprise merge commit on a shared branch. Fetching first, looking at the difference and then merging or rebasing on purpose avoided later confusion.
remotes-fetch-pull-and-push.x: Know exactly what pull does and set it to the behaviour your team wants. Protect main, keep remotes few and named clearly, and be careful with credentials stored on shared machines.

team-workflows-pull-requests-and-reviews.r: A pull request with three thousand changed lines was approved in five minutes because nobody could review it. The next one was split into small steps and caught a real bug on the first read.
team-workflows-pull-requests-and-reviews.x: A workflow is a trade between speed and safety. Prefer small reviewed changes, required checks and clear ownership. Measure review time, because slow review quietly pushes people toward bigger, riskier changes.

tags-releases-and-versioning.r: A hotfix was needed for version 2.3 while main already held unfinished 2.4 work. Because releases were tagged and a branch could be made from the tag, the fix shipped without dragging half-done features along.
tags-releases-and-versioning.x: Releases should be reproducible from a tag. Use semantic versions, generate changelogs from commits, sign tags and decide how long you support old versions before someone asks.

hooks-signing-and-secrets-in-history.r: A cloud key was committed by mistake and removed in the next commit, but it stayed in history and was found by a scanner within hours. The team rotated the key first, then cleaned history, and added a secret-scanning hook.
hooks-signing-and-secrets-in-history.x: Treat a leaked secret as compromised the moment it is pushed: rotate first, rewrite later. Prevent with hooks and server-side scanning, and prefer short-lived credentials so a leak has a small window.

large-repositories-submodules-and-worktr.r: A build agent took twenty minutes just to clone a huge repository. A shallow clone with sparse checkout of only the needed folders cut it to under a minute.
large-repositories-submodules-and-worktr.x: Repository size is an engineering cost that grows quietly. Decide on monorepo or many repositories deliberately, avoid committing binaries, and understand the maintenance burden of submodules.

debugging-git-problems.r: A bug appeared sometime in the last two hundred commits. Bisect found the offending change in eight steps by testing the midpoint each time, and blame showed the reason it had been made.
debugging-git-problems.x: Version control is also a debugging instrument. Keep commits small and the build green so bisect works, and remember the reflog is local and temporary, so recover quickly.
